title: My peace I give (John 14:27)
hookLine: not as the world gives; said at every Mass before the sign of peace

cards: Partway through Mass, a little after the Our Father, strangers turn to each other. A handshake across the pew. A nod to the teenager behind, a hug for a mother, a wave to someone too far away to reach.
Peace be with you. Just before that moment, the priest says a short prayer that recalls a single sentence Jesus spoke at the Last Supper. It goes by quickly.

teach.h: A GOODBYE GIFT AT THE DOOR.
teach.b: Jesus is still at the table, telling his friends he's leaving. He's promised them the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, who will teach them and remind them of everything.
Then, like someone at a doorway saying goodbye, he leaves them a gift.
In the Douay-Rheims: "Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, do I give unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, nor let it be afraid."
Peace, shalom, was an everyday word of greeting; after Easter Jesus will greet these same friends with it: peace be to you. Here he takes that everyday word and fills it. My peace.
Not as the world gives. The world usually gives peace as an absence: no war, no noise, no problems, everything finally sorted out. Peace when the to-do list is done.

Jesus says this to men who are about to watch him arrested, who will scatter in fear and hide behind locked doors. Nothing around them will be calm. Whatever his peace is, it isn't the absence of trouble.
It's given in the middle of it. Perhaps that's why the Church puts it where it does.

teach.h: PEACE IN THE MIDDLE OF TROUBLE.
teach.b: Before the sign of peace, the priest addresses Christ, recalling that he said to the apostles, peace I leave you, my peace I give you, and asks him to look not on our sins but on the faith of his Church.

teach.h: THE PRAYER BEFORE THE SIGN OF PEACE.
teach.b: Then the peace is passed, hand to hand.
Not a feeling people work up, but a gift handed on.

how: At Mass, after the Our Father, the priest prays a prayer recalling John 14:27 and says, "The peace of the Lord be with you always"; then people may exchange a sign of peace with those near them.

o: a calm that comes once all trouble is gone
peace, given even in the middle of trouble
a formal greeting said only by priests

p: given in the middle of it
passed hand to hand at Mass

s: Jesus promised peace because things were about to calm down
he said it the night before his arrest; his friends would scatter.
the prayer before the sign of peace recalls John 14:27
the priest recalls: peace I leave you, my peace I give you.
after Easter, Jesus greets his frightened friends with peace
John 20:19: peace be to you, behind doors shut for fear.

games.q: you're saying goodbye to friends who will soon be frightened and scattered. what do you leave them?
o: your peace, not as the world gives.
a promise that nothing bad will happen.
games.why: Jesus leaves them his peace, and adds: let not your heart be troubled, nor let it be afraid.

practice: Notice whatever is unsettled today, and don't try to fix it; breathe in as if you were being handed something, and out as if you were setting it down.
Then think of one person you're tense with, or haven't spoken to in a while, and picture turning to them, as at Mass, and offering your hand.
If you pray, hold the line, my peace I give unto you; if you don't, just hold the picture.

wordCard.voice: Eirene. The Greek word for peace, standing for shalom: Jesus's farewell gift at the supper, not as the world gives it. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: peace (John 14:27), standing for the Hebrew shalom.

carryVoice: Your line: not as the world gives. Peace comes before things are sorted out, not after. Day five hundred nineteen.
